name: ip_tryforward
prose: Precondition: m is a mbuf with a packet header, a non-NULL receive interface and an IPv4 header, called inside a network epoch; the caller owns m. Postcondition: the function returns either m, still owned by the caller, for full processing in ip_input, or NULL, in which case m has been consumed. It returns m when the IP header length is not the minimum and V_ip_doopts == 1; when m has M_BCAST or M_MCAST set, the receive interface is IFF_LOOPBACK, or the source or destination address is a broadcast, multicast or link-local address; when in_localip_fib says the destination is local; and, after the input pfil hook ran, when the destination address changed to a local address or when M_FASTFWD_OURS is set, and, after the forwarding pfil hook ran, when the destination changed or a forward tag exists and either M_FASTFWD_OURS is set or in_localip says the new destination is local. On every return of m through the forwardlocal label M_FASTFWD_OURS is set on m. It returns NULL, after icmp_error consumed m, when V_ip_doopts == 2 and options are present, when the TTL is at or below IPTTLDEC (skipped when V_ipstealth is on, IPSTEALTH builds), and when ip_findroute fails; it returns NULL after freeing m for a blackhole or broadcast next hop, for a pfil hook verdict other than PFIL_PASS, and when ip_fragment fails. When the packet is forwarded it decrements the TTL (and adjusts ip_sum incrementally unless CSUM_IP is pending), may finish IP, delayed-data or SCTP checksums in software, may build a redirect copy, and hands m (or each fragment) to the next-hop interface's if_output, which consumes it; a DF packet larger than the next-hop MTU gets an ICMP need-fragmentation error instead. If if_output fails for a fragment, the remaining unsent fragments are freed. The function returns NULL in all of these forwarded cases.
note: Slice 255-547 starts inside the function; the real definition is ip_tryforward at ip_fastfwd.c:237 (no function named ip_forward in this file), tail 548-588 read from the file. Returns listed from lines 265,269,292,298,333/339/439 (forwardlocal), 359,399,452,583,587.

name: icmp_error
prose: Precondition: n is a mbuf chain holding the received IP datagram that triggered the error (n is dereferenced without a NULL check), type is at most ICMP_MAXTYPE (KASSERT), and code, dest and mtu describe the ICMP error. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and consumes n on every path, by m_freem(n) at the freeit label (n may by then be a replacement chain from m_pullup, or NULL after a failed m_pullup, which freed the chain). No ICMP message is sent when n has M_DECRYPTED, M_BCAST or M_MCAST set; when the first mbuf holds fewer than sizeof(struct ip) + ICMP_MINLEN bytes or fewer than the IP header length + ICMP_MINLEN bytes; when ip_off has any bit besides IP_MF and IP_DF set (a non-first fragment); when the datagram is an ICMP message of a non-informational type and the error type is not ICMP_REDIRECT; for TCP when an m_pullup fails, the TCP header length is below sizeof(struct tcphdr) or ntohs(ip_len) is smaller than the IP plus TCP header length; for SCTP when an m_pullup fails; when the computed quoted length icmplen is below sizeof(struct ip); and when mbuf allocation fails. Where the quoted headers are not contiguous in a single-mbuf chain (TCP) or the SCTP ip_len is smaller than the IP plus SCTP common header, the code takes the stdreply path and still sends the error, quoting at least 8 bytes up to V_icmp_quotelen. Otherwise it builds a new ICMP mbuf of the requested type and code, quoting the original header and data, and passes it to icmp_reflect, which takes ownership of the new mbuf.
note: Reviewer right: SCTP branch goto stdreply at ip_icmp.c:294-298 sends a reply when ip_len is inconsistent; TCP ip_len inconsistency (line 280-281) does goto freeit, so old claim 'inconsistent ip_len -> nothing sent' was wrong for SCTP. Slice 269-523 cuts the head (function at line 215).

name: icmp_input
prose: Precondition: called inside a network epoch with *mp pointing to a mbuf chain holding an IPv4 packet whose ICMP message starts at byte offset *offp; the caller's reference to the chain is passed to the function. The function sets *mp to NULL on entry. Postcondition: it returns IPPROTO_DONE on every return (lines 499, 583, 667, 764, 768) and consumes the mbuf exactly once. It frees the mbuf with m_freem when the ICMP length is below ICMP_MINLEN, when the ICMP checksum fails, when a problem-datagram notification (unreachable, time exceeded, parameter problem) is shorter than ICMP_ADVLENMIN or ICMP_ADVLEN, or has an inner IP header length below the minimum, or has an INADDR_ANY inner source or destination, and when badport_bandlim rejects an echo or timestamp request. After a failed m_pullup (two places) it returns with the chain already freed by m_pullup. For answered echo, timestamp and mask requests it passes the mbuf to icmp_reflect and returns. On all other paths (message types above ICMP_MAXTYPE; unreachable, time exceeded or parameter-problem notifications with a bad code or a multicast inner destination, which are only counted as bad codes; delivered notifications, after ip_stripoptions and an optional ip_ctlprotox call for the inner protocol; ignored echo or timestamp requests; mask requests that are not answered; redirects, which may be installed in every FIB through rib_add_redirect; and reply or unknown types) it stores the mbuf, possibly re-pulled-up, in *mp and calls rip_input, which takes ownership; *mp is not left pointing at the mbuf on any freed path.
note: Reviewer right: old prose said *mp both holds the chain on entry and is NULL on entry; code sets *mp = NULL at line 476 and sets *mp = m only at label raw (762). Return IPPROTO_DONE at lines 499,583,667,764,768 confirmed. Slice 524-785 cuts the head (function at 461).

name: ip_input
prose: Precondition: m has a packet header and the caller is inside a network epoch (M_ASSERTPKTHDR, NET_EPOCH_ASSERT). Postcondition: the function returns nothing and takes over ownership of m: on every path m is either freed here or handed to another routine (ip_tryforward, pfil hooks, ip_forward, ip_dooptions, ip_reass, IPSEC_INPUT or the ip_protox handler). If M_FASTFWD_OURS is set on entry the flag is cleared and processing jumps straight to local delivery without the checks below. Otherwise it frees m (counting the matching IPSTAT counter) when the packet is shorter than an IP header, a pullup fails, the version is not 4, the header length is below the minimum, a loopback source or destination arrives on a non-loopback interface, the header checksum is wrong, ip_len is below the header length or above the packet length, the destination is INADDR_ANY, ip_dooptions reports an error, the strong-ES check or source-address validation fails for a matching local address, a multicast packet is rejected by ip_mforward, the destination or source is link-local and the destination is neither a local, broadcast nor multicast address, or the packet is not for this host and V_ipforwarding is 0. A pfil input hook verdict other than PFIL_PASS, a failed ip_reass, or a nonzero IPSEC_INPUT result also end processing with the mbuf already consumed by the callee. Packets destined elsewhere are passed to ip_forward (also for an ipfw forward tag); multicast packets are given to ip_mforward only when multicast routing is enabled and the source is not link-local, and are otherwise accepted for local delivery. Local packets run the local pfil hook, are reassembled when ip_off has MF or an offset, and are delivered through ip_protox[ip->ip_p].
note: Reviewer right: link-local multicast source does not drop the packet, it skips ip_mforward (line 768-769) and falls to 'goto ours' (799). Slice 515-783 cuts the head (function at 457).

name: ip_ctloutput
prose: Precondition: so has an inpcb and sopt describes a socket option request. Postcondition: returns an errno value, 0 on success, with the inpcb lock not held on return (each acquisition is released inside the same case). For sopt_level != IPPROTO_IP it returns EINVAL unless the request is a SOPT_SET at SOL_SOCKET: SO_SETFIB reads an int (error from sooptcopyin returned), returns EISCONN if INP_BOUNDFIB is set and the value differs from so_fibnum, else returns sosetfib's result and, on success, stores the fib in inp_inc.inc_fibnum; SO_MAX_PACING_RATE returns 0 when RATELIMIT is compiled in and EOPNOTSUPP otherwise; other SOL_SOCKET names return EINVAL. For level IPPROTO_IP with SOPT_SET it handles IP_OPTIONS (EMSGSIZE if sopt_valsize > MLEN, ENOBUFS if m_get fails, sooptcopyin errors, otherwise the mbuf is passed to ip_pcbopts and its result is returned), IP_BINDANY (priv_check error when sopt_td is set), the integer options (EINVAL for an IP_MINTTL outside 0..MAXTTL or an IP_VLAN_PCP outside -1..the PCP mask), IP_PORTRANGE (EINVAL for an unknown value), the multicast options (result of inp_setmoptions) and IP_IPSEC_POLICY (IPSEC_PCBCTL when IPSEC is enabled); any other name returns ENOPROTOOPT. With SOPT_GET it handles IP_OPTIONS and IP_RETOPTS (ENOMEM if m_copym fails, otherwise the sooptcopyout result, or a zero-length value when no options are set), the integer options (value copied out with sooptcopyout, whose result is the return value), the multicast get options (inp_getmoptions), IP_IPSEC_POLICY, and ENOPROTOOPT otherwise. An unrecognised sopt_dir returns 0. When RSS is compiled in, a failed rss_hash2bucket sets EINVAL for IP_RSSBUCKETID but the following sooptcopyout assignment overwrites it, so that error is not returned.
note: Reviewer right: rss_hash2bucket failure sets error = EINVAL (ip_output.c:1505) but line 1520 'error = sooptcopyout(...)' overwrites it; old prose said it is propagated. Slice 1312-1565 cuts the head (function at 1095).

name: ip_output
prose: Precondition: m has a packet header and an IPv4 header, the caller is inside a network epoch and holds inp's lock when inp is non-NULL; opt may be NULL, ro may be NULL or a caller-owned route cache, imo may be NULL. Postcondition: the function consumes m on every path (it frees m itself, or passes it to ip_output_send, IPSEC_OUTPUT, a pfil hook, ip_mforward or ip_fragment) and returns an errno or 0. It returns 0 after sending, when IPSEC_OUTPUT returns EINPROGRESS (mapped to 0), and when a multicast packet is freed because ip_mforward returned nonzero, because its TTL is 0 or because the interface is a loopback interface. It returns EHOSTUNREACH when no route exists (and, with IPsec compiled in, no SPD handling follows), ENETUNREACH when IP_SENDONES or IP_ROUTETOIF finds no interface or a multicast destination goes to an interface without IFF_MULTICAST, EADDRNOTAVAIL when a broadcast address is used on an interface without IFF_BROADCAST or a loopback address would leave through a non-loopback interface, EACCES for a broadcast without IP_ALLOWBROADCAST, EMSGSIZE for a broadcast longer than the MTU or when the datagram exceeds the MTU and has DF set or needs TSO, the error of ip_fragment, ip_output_send, a pfil hook or IPSEC_OUTPUT, and the error of mb_unmapped_to_ext, which is EINVAL (a diagnostic is printed), ENOBUFS in place of ENOMEM, or whatever other errno it returns, in which case this function does not free m itself. A caller-supplied ro is filled in and any nexthop reference stored in it is left for the caller; when ro is NULL an on-stack cache is used whose lookup takes no reference, and nothing is released at the exit.
note: Reviewer right: mb_unmapped_to_ext error path (ip_output.c:748-757) returns EINVAL/ENOBUFS/other and does 'goto done' without m_freem; old prose said ENOBUFS only. The old claim 'NULL ro causes the internal route cache to be released before return' is not in the code: done: only returns error (line 863-864); the iproute branch uses fib4_lookup with NHR_NONE (line 519). Slice 519-774 cuts the head (function at 318).

name: IcmpAliasIn
prose: Precondition: la is a libalias instance whose lock the caller holds (LIBALIAS_LOCK_ASSERT) and pip points to an IP packet whose payload is read as an ICMP message; dlen is ntohs(pip->ip_len) minus the IP header length. Postcondition: it returns PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED if dlen < ICMP_MINLEN; then PKT_ALIAS_OK without touching the packet if PKT_ALIAS_PROXY_ONLY is set in la->packetAliasMode; otherwise it dispatches on icmp_type. For ICMP_ECHOREPLY and ICMP_TSTAMPREPLY it returns the result of IcmpAliasIn1 when icmp_code is 0 and PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED when it is not. For ICMP_UNREACH, ICMP_SOURCEQUENCH, ICMP_TIMXCEED and ICMP_PARAMPROB it returns PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED if dlen < ICMP_ADVLENMIN or dlen < ICMP_ADVLEN(ic), and otherwise the result of IcmpAliasIn2. For ICMP_ECHO and ICMP_TSTAMP it returns the result of IcmpAliasIn1 whatever the code is. Any other type returns PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED. IcmpAliasIn1 returns the FindIcmpIn status, and on PKT_ALIAS_OK it restores the ICMP id and the IP destination address with checksum updates; IcmpAliasIn2 returns PKT_ALIAS_OK after rewriting the embedded packet and outer destination, the FindUdpTcpIn or FindIcmpIn error status, or PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED when no link applies. The function takes no lock and frees nothing.
note: Checked against alias.c:437-479, IcmpAliasIn1 (288-325) and IcmpAliasIn2 (331-435); both early reviewer objections (proxy-only return, lnk==NULL IGNORED) are covered. Slice 255-508 cuts the head (function at 437).

name: IcmpAliasOut
prose: Precondition: la is locked by the caller (LIBALIAS_LOCK_ASSERT) and pip points to an outgoing IP packet whose payload is read as an ICMP header; create is only forwarded to IcmpAliasOut1. Postcondition: if PKT_ALIAS_PROXY_ONLY is set in la->packetAliasMode it returns PKT_ALIAS_OK without touching the packet. Otherwise it dispatches on icmp_type: ICMP_ECHO and ICMP_TSTAMP with icmp_code == 0 return the result of IcmpAliasOut1(la, pip, create), with a nonzero code they return PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED; ICMP_UNREACH, ICMP_SOURCEQUENCH, ICMP_TIMXCEED and ICMP_PARAMPROB return the result of IcmpAliasOut2(la, pip); ICMP_ECHOREPLY and ICMP_TSTAMPREPLY return the result of IcmpAliasOut1(la, pip, create) whatever the code is; any other type returns PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED. The status values returned are those the callees return (PKT_ALIAS_OK, PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED or the error status of their FindIcmpOut or FindUdpTcpOut lookups); IcmpAliasOut itself takes no lock and allocates and frees no memory.
note: Checked against alias.c:634-668: create is passed to IcmpAliasOut1 (lines 654, 665), so earlier claim that it is unused was wrong; no path returns PKT_ALIAS_RAW from this function itself. Slice 509-764 cuts the head (function at 634).

name: ProtoAliasOut
prose: Precondition: la is locked by the caller (LIBALIAS_LOCK_ASSERT), pip points to an outgoing IP packet, ip_sum points to its IP header checksum field and ip_dst and ip_p describe the destination address and protocol. Postcondition: if PKT_ALIAS_PROXY_ONLY is set in la->packetAliasMode it returns PKT_ALIAS_OK without changing the packet (this test comes before the create test, so it also applies when create is 0); otherwise if create is 0 it returns PKT_ALIAS_IGNORED without changing the packet; otherwise it calls FindProtoOut(la, pip->ip_src, ip_dst, ip_p, &lnk) and returns its status. Only when that status is PKT_ALIAS_OK it takes GetAliasAddress(lnk), updates the checksum at ip_sum with DifferentialChecksum and replaces pip->ip_src with the alias address; for any other status the packet is left unchanged. The function takes no lock and allocates and frees no memory.
note: Checked against alias.c:707-735: proxy-only test (717) precedes !create (720), so !create can return PKT_ALIAS_OK; reviewer point already reflected. Slice 509-764 cuts the head (function at 707).

name: AliasHandleRtspOut
prose: Precondition: la, pip and lnk describe an outgoing TCP segment of an RTSP connection (pip points to an IP packet whose TCP header follows the IP header) and maxlen is the buffer size available for the packet. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It computes the header length and ntohs(pip->ip_len) and returns without changes if the header length exceeds the total length or the total length exceeds maxlen. Otherwise, when the TCP destination port is RTSP_CONTROL_PORT_NUMBER_1 or RTSP_CONTROL_PORT_NUMBER_2 (client direction) it calls alias_rtsp_out with the string client_port if the data begins with SETUP and then returns, or calls alias_pna_out with the data length if the data begins with PNA; other client data is left alone. For any other destination port (server direction) it returns unchanged if the data is shorter than the 200 plus OK minimum, and otherwise scans for the text 200 followed by blanks and OK and calls alias_rtsp_out with the string server_port for the first such match, after which the scan stops; without a match nothing is changed. Packet rewriting is done only inside alias_rtsp_out and alias_pna_out.
note: Slice cut the head: the excerpt 506-545 is the tail of static void AliasHandleRtspOut (alias_smedia.c:487-545); the dropped excerpt name was not a function name, the function exists, so fixed under its real name.

name: rip_send
prose: Precondition: so has a raw IP inpcb (KASSERT), m is a mbuf chain with a packet header, and control (if any) is passed to the function. Postcondition: the function consumes control (always freed if non-NULL) and m, and returns an errno or the result of ip_output. If the socket is connected and nam is given it frees m and returns EISCONN. If it is not connected it frees m and returns ENOTCONN (no nam), EAFNOSUPPORT (family not AF_INET) or EINVAL (sa_len not sizeof(struct sockaddr_in)). Without INP_HDRINCL it frees m and returns EMSGSIZE if the chain plus an IP header exceeds IP_MAXPACKET, returns ENOBUFS if M_PREPEND fails (m already freed by it), then builds an IP header from the inpcb under an inp read lock; if the socket is jailed and the source is INADDR_ANY it takes the address from in_pcbladdr, otherwise it checks it with prison_local_ip4, and on error it unlocks, frees m and returns that error. With INP_HDRINCL it frees m and returns EMSGSIZE for a chain above IP_MAXPACKET or EINVAL for one shorter than struct ip, returns ENOMEM when the first m_pullup fails and EINVAL when the second one (for the full header length) fails (m_pullup frees the chain), then takes the inp read lock and frees m with EINVAL when the header length is below the minimum, user options are given while inp_options is set or ntohs(ip_len) differs from the chain length, returns the prison_check_ip4 error for the source address, and returns EINVAL for a malformed option list; every one of those exits unlocks the read lock first. Finally it calls ip_output(m, inp->inp_options, NULL, flags, inp->inp_moptions, inp) inside a network epoch, releases the inp read lock and returns ip_output's result; ip_output consumes m.
note: Slice 515-769 starts in the middle of the function; the real name is rip_send (raw_ip.c:442-648), no function rip_output exists in this file. Reviewed every return: 465,479,494,498,540,547,551,555,561,585,591,611,618,647.

name: sctp_asconf_queue_add
prose: Precondition: stcb is a valid association control block, ifa is a local address and type is SCTP_ADD_IP_ADDRESS, SCTP_DEL_IP_ADDRESS or SCTP_SET_PRIM_ADDR. Postcondition: it returns -1 without changes when the peer does not support ASCONF (asoc.asconf_supported == 0). When type is SCTP_DEL_IP_ADDRESS and asconf_del_pending is not set and ifa is the last local address (sctp_local_addr_count is 0 for a bound-all endpoint, 1 otherwise), it records the delete as pending (asconf_del_pending = 1, asconf_addr_del_pending = ifa, ifa refcount incremented) and returns -1 without queueing. In every other case it calls sctp_asconf_queue_mgmt, which returns 0 when it queued the parameter and -1 when it did not (a same-type unsent entry for that address exists, an add cancelled a queued unsent delete or a delete cancelled a queued unsent add, memory allocation failed, or the address family is unsupported, in which case the reference it took on ifa is dropped); this value is returned, except that when type is SCTP_ADD_IP_ADDRESS, the queueing returned 0 and a delete is pending, it also queues the pending delete: if that second call returns 0 the pending-delete state is cleared and its ifa reference dropped, the congestion parameters, RTO and error count of every net and the association's overall error count are reset, an advisory SCTP_SET_PRIM_ADDR for ifa is queued, and the function returns 1 so that the caller sends the ASCONF at once; if the second call does not return 0 the function returns 0 and the pending delete stays set. A SCTP_DEL_IP_ADDRESS or SCTP_SET_PRIM_ADDR request made while a delete is already pending is queued normally.
note: Reviewer (r15) wrong: 'with a pending delete and type != ADD it returns -1 without queueing' - code at sctp_asconf.c:1354 only skips the pending branch, then 1372 calls sctp_asconf_queue_mgmt for every type. The r2 point (last-address branch needs !asconf_del_pending) is already stated. Also sctp_asconf_queue_mgmt returns -1 when an add cancels a queued delete (1243) and vice versa (1254), not only for duplicates. Slice 1107-1370 cuts the head (function at 1337).

name: sctp_addr_mgmt_ep_sa
prose: Precondition: inp and sa are valid; type is SCTP_ADD_IP_ADDRESS or SCTP_DEL_IP_ADDRESS (any other value finds no address); vrf_id selects the VRF used to look up an address to add. Postcondition: returns a uint32_t errno value, 0 on success. It returns EINVAL if sa->sa_len is 0. For an add it looks the address up on the system with sctp_find_ifa_by_addr, for a delete in the endpoint with sctp_find_ifa_in_ep, and returns EADDRNOTAVAIL if no address is found or type is neither. For an add it calls sctp_add_local_addr_ep; for a delete it returns EINVAL when inp->laddr_count is below 2, otherwise it marks the matching sctp_laddr entries with the delete action. If the endpoint has no associations a delete then removes the matching entries immediately with sctp_del_local_addr_ep (an add needs nothing more); if it has associations, for an add as well as a delete, it allocates an iterator work item (ENOMEM if the iterator structure or the laddr work item cannot be allocated), takes an extra reference on ifa, starts an iterator with sctp_initiate_iterator, returns EFAULT after calling sctp_asconf_iterator_end on the work item if the iterator cannot be started, and otherwise returns 0 with the reference released later by the iterator end routine. The ENOMEM and EFAULT returns happen after the local address list has already been changed (the add was registered, or the delete action was marked on the entry).
note: Old prose wrongly restricted the iterator to deletes and said no change is applied on error; sctp_asconf.c:3194-3209 changes the endpoint list before the allocation and iterator steps (3210-3261). Slice 3180-3473 cuts the head (function at 3173).

name: sctp_delayed_cksum
prose: Precondition: m is a mbuf chain with a packet header (M_ASSERTPKTHDR in sctp_calculate_cksum) and offset, the offset of the SCTP common header, is below m->m_pkthdr.len (KASSERT in sctp_calculate_cksum). Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It first computes the CRC32c SCTP checksum over the bytes from offset to the end of the chain with sctp_calculate_cksum, then applies SCTP_STAT_DECR(sctps_sendhwcrc) and SCTP_STAT_INCR(sctps_sendswcrc), then adds offsetof(struct sctphdr, checksum) to its local offset exactly once. If this advanced offset plus sizeof(uint32_t) exceeds m->m_pkthdr.len it panics when INVARIANTS is compiled in and otherwise prints a diagnostic with SCTP_PRINTF and returns without writing; in both cases the checksum was already computed. Otherwise it writes the 4-byte checksum into the chain with m_copyback at the advanced offset, which is the position of the checksum field of the SCTP common header.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose counted offsetof twice; code at sctp_crc32.c:122-134 adds it once and uses the advanced offset for both the bounds test and m_copyback. Slice 1-136 covers the whole function (starts at 114) but with a wrong earlier prose.

name: sctp_queue_data_for_reasm
prose: Precondition: control and chk belong to asoc (control->sinfo_stream indexes asoc->strmin), tsn is the TSN of chk, created_control says whether the caller just allocated control, and abort_flag points to the caller's flag. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and leaves the TCB lock to the caller. If created_control is set it increments asoc->cnt_on_all_streams when the chunk is ordered or asoc->idata_supported is set, then calls sctp_place_control_in_stream; when that reports a duplicate it calls sctp_abort_in_reasm, sctp_clean_up_control on control and returns; and when idata is not supported, tsn equals asoc->cumulative_tsn + 1 and chk lacks SCTP_DATA_FIRST_FRAG it calls sctp_abort_in_reasm and returns. Then, when idata is not supported and the chunk is unordered, it calls sctp_inject_old_unordered_data and returns without queueing chk here. If chk has FIRST_FRAG it calls sctp_abort_in_reasm and returns when control->first_frag_seen is already set; otherwise it sets first_frag_seen, sinfo_ppid, sinfo_tsn and fsn_included from chk, moves chk->data into control->data, marks the TSN non-revokable, frees chk, sets the tail pointer and adds control->length to asoc->size_on_all_streams. For a chunk without FIRST_FRAG it, when last_frag_seen is clear, raises top_fsn to the chunk's fsn if larger and, for a LAST_FRAG chunk, sets last_frag_seen and aborts when top_fsn is then greater than the chunk's fsn; when last_frag_seen is already set it aborts for a second LAST_FRAG chunk or an fsn above top_fsn; in both cases it also aborts when (idata_supported or first_frag_seen) and control->fsn_included is at or after the chunk's fsn; each abort calls sctp_abort_in_reasm (which may set *abort_flag) and returns. Otherwise it walks control->reasm: a chunk with a greater fsn found first makes it abort if chk is LAST_FRAG, and otherwise inserts chk before that entry; an equal fsn aborts; if neither occurs it appends chk at the tail; an inserted chunk adds send_size to asoc->size_on_reasm_queue and increments asoc->cnt_on_reasm_queue. Finally, if control->first_frag_seen, it moves consecutive entries (fsn equal to fsn_included + 1, then onward) into the control with sctp_add_chk_to_control, setting do_wakeup if the control is on the read queue and otherwise adding the added length to size_on_all_streams; when control->end_added and control->pdapi_started are both set it clears pdapi_started (and strm->pd_api_started) if strm->pd_api_started was set, adds control to the read queue if it is not on it, and stops; it calls sctp_wakeup_the_read_socket if do_wakeup was set.
note: Reviewer (r15) right: the created-control case at cumulative_tsn+1 without FIRST_FRAG aborts and returns (sctp_indata.c:1386-1398), which the old prose omitted. Other claims (old unordered inject returns without abort; not reached after failed placement) are consistent with lines 1378-1403. Slice 1185-1441 cuts the head (function at 1351).

name: sctp_handle_sack
prose: Precondition: the TCB lock on stcb is held (SCTP_TCB_LOCK_ASSERT), stcb and its association are valid, m holds the SACK gap-ack and duplicate-TSN blocks when num_seg, num_nr_seg or num_dup are nonzero, and cum_ack and rwnd come from the received SACK. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It first zeroes asoc.overall_error_count. If cum_ack is at or beyond the next TSN to send (the last sent_queue TSN plus one, or sending_seq if the queue is empty) it sets *abort_now to 1 and aborts the association with sctp_abort_an_association before returning. If asoc->last_acked_seq is strictly newer than cum_ack it returns at once (so a SACK with cum_ack equal to last_acked_seq is processed further). If the sent queue, send queue and stream queue are all empty it sets peers_rwnd from rwnd (set to 0 when below the SWS sender threshold), clears the retransmit count, stops the send timer on each net, zeroes flight and partial-bytes counters and returns. name: sctp_kick_prsctp_reorder_queue
prose: Precondition: stcb is non-NULL (KASSERT), the TCB lock on stcb and the endpoint read lock are held, and strmin is a stream input queue of stcb's association. name: sctp_process_cookie_existing
prose: Precondition: the TCB lock on stcb is held by the caller (stcb is non-NULL), m holds a COOKIE-ECHO chunk containing the cookie, offset locates that chunk, netp points to the association's current destination, and init_src, notification and the other arguments are valid. name: sctp_process_control

name: sctp_send_str_reset_req
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the TCB lock on stcb (SCTP_TCB_LOCK_ASSERT); number_entries and list describe the streams of an incoming-reset request. name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket; message data is supplied either through uio or, when uio is NULL, through the mbuf chain top (neither supplied gives EINVAL); addr, control and srcv are optional; the caller holds no TCB lock. name: sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: inp is the endpoint; stcb and net may be NULL; to is the destination sockaddr; m is a mbuf chain holding an SCTP common header and chunks but no IP header, and the function takes ownership of m. Postcondition: it returns 0 when the lower layer reports success, otherwise an errno, and m has been consumed in every case (freed here on the early error returns, passed to ip_output or ip6_output otherwise). It returns EFAULT, after freeing m, when net is non-NULL with SCTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_SCOPE set and when the destination address family is neither AF_INET nor AF_INET6 (or the family is not compiled in). When auth and stcb are both non-NULL it first fills in the AUTH chunk's HMAC digest. For AF_INET it prepends an IP header (plus a UDP header when port is nonzero), returning ENOMEM if the header mbuf cannot be allocated, EHOSTUNREACH if the cached source address is unusable and no other can be chosen, if source address selection fails, if the UDP tunneling port is 0 while port is set, or if a route cannot be obtained, and ENOMEM if SCTP_GET_HEADER_FOR_OUTPUT cannot prepend the output header; it computes the SCTP checksum in software for UDP-encapsulated packets and otherwise sets CSUM_SCTP for offload, calls ip_output and returns its result. For AF_INET6 it does the same with an IPv6 header, additionally returning EINVAL for some address-scope failures, the error of sa6_recoverscope, and the result of ip6_output. After the send it updates statistics, frees a temporary route when net is NULL, and may lower net->mtu and call sctp_pathmtu_adjustment when the route reports a smaller path MTU.

name: sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters
prose: Precondition: in_initpkt is a mbuf chain holding an INIT or INIT-ACK chunk (cp points at its chunk header), param_offset is the offset of its first parameter, abort_processing and nat_friendly point to writable ints (nat_friendly is written without a NULL check), and cookie_found and edmid may be NULL. The function walks the parameters while at least a parameter header of bytes remains, and returns a mbuf chain of operational error causes or NULL (also NULL when allocation of the error mbuf fails). A parameter whose length is above the remaining length or below the header size, or whose padded size is invalid for its known type, sets *abort_processing to 1, frees any error chain built so far and returns a protocol-violation cause mbuf naming the type and length (or NULL if no parameter header could be read or the allocation fails). An SCTP_HOSTNAME_ADDRESS parameter sets *abort_processing to 1, discards the earlier chain and returns an unresolvable-address cause containing the parameter (or NULL if allocation or the copy fails). A parameter of an unknown type with the 0x4000 report bit adds an unrecognised-parameter cause to the chain (the chain is freed and discarded on allocation failure); with the 0x8000 bit clear the walk stops and the chain built so far is returned with *abort_processing still 0; with it set the parameter is skipped and the walk continues. Reaching the end of the parameters returns the chain, possibly NULL.

name: sctp_send_initiate_ack
prose: Precondition: inp is the endpoint, stcb is NULL or an association (when non-NULL its TCB lock is held and is temporarily released and reacquired while picking a new tag), init_pkt and init_chk locate the received INIT chunk, src, dst, sh and the flow arguments describe the received packet. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and sends at most one INIT-ACK. It builds the INIT-ACK itself in a newly allocated mbuf, together with the state cookie, and consumes that mbuf in every case: it frees it and sends nothing when the INIT-ACK mbuf, a pad mbuf or the cookie cannot be allocated or the socket is gone (inp->sctp_socket is NULL), when source address selection fails for the association's destination, and when sctp_add_cookie fails. When stcb exists in a state other than COOKIE_WAIT it instead sends an ABORT, without building an INIT-ACK, if the INIT carries addresses new to the association or the remote encapsulation port changed; it also sends an ABORT, with a generated cause if none exists, if sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters sets abort_flag or if the address family is not AF_INET or AF_INET6. name: sctp_med_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: the TCB lock on stcb is held (SCTP_TCB_LOCK_ASSERT), inp, stcb and asoc are valid, num_out and reason_code point to writable ints, now and now_filled describe a timestamp cache the function may fill in, and control_only, from_where, frag_point and so_locked are as supplied by the caller. Postcondition: *num_out is set to 0 and *reason_code to 0 on entry; the function returns 0 on every path except three ENOMEM returns (at lines 8160, 8387 and 8737, with *reason_code set to 8, 8 and 3 respectively). It returns 0 with *reason_code 9 when there is nothing to send (control queue empty or only ECN-echo chunks, no ASCONF chunks, send queue or unsent stream data), and 0 with *reason_code 8 when the control, ASCONF and send queues are all empty at the later check at line 7988. Otherwise it walks the destinations, bundles control chunks, ASCONF chunks and eligible data chunks into packets limited by the MTU, cwnd and peer window, and sends each packet with sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output. A failed lower-level send is not returned: it counts statistics, sets asoc->ifp_had_enobuf for ENOBUFS, moves chunks away from the destination for EHOSTUNREACH, records *reason_code 6 or 7 and moves on; at the end *reason_code is overwritten with 4 (nothing was sent and the code was still 0) or 5, so the final value is 4 or 5 unless the function returned earlier. *num_out counts chunks sent, *now and *now_filled are filled in when a timestamp is needed, sctp_clean_up_ctl is called before the normal return, and the TCB lock stays held. The local variable quit_now is not an output of this function.

name: sctp_load_addresses_from_init
prose: Precondition: stcb is a locked association; m is the packet and offset points at the first parameter of an INIT or INIT-ACK whose parameters end at limit; src, dst and altsa (an alternate source address that replaces src when non-NULL) and port describe the received packet. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and a negative value otherwise; the distinct negative values (-1 to -35, -100, -101) identify the failing step. It marks every existing net SCTP_ADDR_NOT_IN_ASSOC, adds the source address as a remote address if no association exists for it (returns -1 or -2 if sctp_add_remote_addr fails, -3 if the address belongs to another association, in which case that association's lock is released, and -4 if stcb->asoc.state is 0), then walks the parameters: it adds IPv4 and IPv6 addresses as remote addresses (clearing the not-in-association mark of ones already known and returning other negative values for failures such as an address owned by another association or a failed sctp_add_remote_addr), records supported features (ECN, PR-SCTP, auth, ASCONF, reconfig, NR-SACK, packet-drop, IDATA), takes the RANDOM, HMAC and CHUNK list parameters (returning negative values for malformed ones), and stops the walk at an unknown parameter whose upper bit is clear. Afterwards it removes remote addresses still marked not-in-association (reselecting the primary destination), turns off locally enabled features that the peer did not advertise, returns -31, -32 or -33 for inconsistent authentication or ASCONF parameters, builds the peer random key and installs it in asoc.authinfo.peer_random, returning -34 if the key cannot be allocated, clears the cached keys and returns 0.

name: sys_sctp_generic_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: td is the calling thread and uap holds the user's descriptor, iovec array, optional sinfo, from, fromlenaddr and msg_flags pointers. Postcondition: the function returns an errno or 0, with the received byte count stored in td->td_retval[0] on the success paths. It returns getsock's error without dropping a file reference; returns the copyiniov error (EMSGSIZE limit) after dropping the file reference; after the iovec has been allocated every exit frees iov, and every exit after a successful getsock drops the file reference with fdrop. It returns EOPNOTSUPP if the socket is not an SCTP socket, the mac_socket_check_receive error with MAC, the copyin error for fromlenaddr or msg_flags, and EINVAL if the sum of the iov lengths overflows. It then calls sctp_sorecvmsg; if that returns an error and some data was already received and the error is ERESTART, EINTR or EWOULDBLOCK, the error is cleared; any other error is returned. When sctp_sorecvmsg returned 0 it copies sinfo out when uap->sinfo is set, returning the copyout error; this copy is skipped when the error was converted to 0 above. On success it sets td_retval[0] to the number of bytes received, copies the source address (truncated to the user's length) and its length out when fromlen and uap->from are set, and copies msg_flags out when uap->msg_flags is set, returning the first copyout error.

name: sctp_threshold_management
prose: Precondition: stcb is non-NULL with its TCB lock held (KASSERT and SCTP_TCB_LOCK_ASSERT), inp is its endpoint, net may be NULL, and threshold is the association error limit. Postcondition: if net is non-NULL its error_count is incremented. When it then exceeds net->failure_threshold and SCTP_ADDR_REACHABLE is set in net->dest_state, SCTP_ADDR_REACHABLE, SCTP_ADDR_REQ_PRIMARY and SCTP_ADDR_PF are cleared and an interface-down notification is delivered; if it exceeds the threshold but the address is not marked reachable, nothing more happens to the destination state. Otherwise, when net->pf_threshold is below net->failure_threshold, error_count exceeds pf_threshold and SCTP_ADDR_PF is not set, SCTP_ADDR_PF is set, last_active is updated, a heartbeat is sent and the heartbeat timer is stopped and restarted. For a non-NULL net stcb->asoc.overall_error_count is incremented only if SCTP_ADDR_UNCONFIRMED is not set in net->dest_state; for a NULL net it is always incremented. If overall_error_count then exceeds threshold the association is aborted with sctp_abort_an_association and the function returns 1 (the caller must not use stcb afterwards); otherwise it returns 0.

name: sctp_getopt
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket; optval is a buffer of at least the size required by optname and *optsize holds its size. Postcondition: the function returns an errno value, 0 on success. It returns EINVAL at once, without touching *optsize, if optval is NULL or so->so_pcb is NULL. Otherwise it dispatches on optname: for each recognised option it checks the buffer size with SCTP_CHECK_AND_CAST (EINVAL if too small), finds the association where required (SCTP_FIND_STCB) and fills the buffer with the option value taking the appropriate lock, setting *optsize to the size of the option structure on success; options that need a bound-all endpoint, an association or a particular socket type give EINVAL otherwise, and an unrecognised optname gives ENOPROTOOPT. Any nonzero error causes *optsize to be set to 0 before the single return at the end; the buffer contents are then unspecified.

Returns verified: 1514, 1520, 3715 (only three returns); error => *optsize = 0 (3712-3714). Old claim '*optsize unchanged on error' was wrong. Per-option details not enumerated.

name: sctp_setopt
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket; optval points to optsize bytes of option data and p is the calling thread. Postcondition: the function returns an errno value, 0 on success. It returns EINVAL at once if optval is NULL or so->so_pcb is NULL. Otherwise it dispatches on optname; for each recognised option it checks the buffer size with SCTP_CHECK_AND_CAST (EINVAL when too small), locates the association by id where the option is per-association, and updates either the endpoint defaults or the association (or all associations) under the corresponding lock. Several cases return directly: EPERM for SCTP_AUTO_ASCONF set to a nonzero value while the auto_asconf sysctl is off, EINVAL for SCTP_AUTO_ASCONF on a socket that is not bound-all, SCTP_I_WANT_MAPPED_V4_ADDR on a socket that is not bound to IPv6, SCTP_AUTOCLOSE on a TCP-style socket, and EINVAL for SCTP_PEER_ADDR_PARAMS with both heartbeat enable and disable flags, both PMTU-discovery flags, or a path MTU outside SCTP_SMALLEST_PMTU..SCTP_LARGEST_PMTU with PMTU discovery disabled; in those cases the TCB lock taken so far is released. An unrecognised optname returns ENOPROTOOPT; other failures return the error assigned in the case (for example EINVAL, EAFNOSUPPORT, ENOENT). The function returns the final value of error.

name: sctp_shutdown
prose: Precondition: so is a socket whose so_pcb is an SCTP endpoint (MPASS) and how is SHUT_RD, SHUT_WR or SHUT_RDWR. Postcondition: it returns EOPNOTSUPP, without waking waiters, if the endpoint is neither SCTP_PCB_FLAGS_TCPTYPE nor SCTP_PCB_FLAGS_IN_TCPPOOL; it returns ENOTCONN, also without waking waiters, if the socket is listening (setting so_error to ECONNABORTED and waking listeners unless how is SHUT_WR) or is none of connected, connecting or disconnecting. Otherwise, for SHUT_RD and SHUT_RDWR it sets SCTP_PCB_FLAGS_SOCKET_CANT_READ and empties the endpoint's read queue: each control is unlinked, its mbufs are accounted off the socket buffer, and, when the control is not on a stream queue, the control and its data are freed, while a control that is still on a stream queue is not freed and, if an association exists, its length is added back to size_on_all_streams; if any control that is not a notification was discarded and an association exists it aborts that association and returns ECONNABORTED; otherwise it calls sorflush and, for SHUT_RD, returns 0. For SHUT_WR, or SHUT_RDWR continuing, it calls socantsendmore and does nothing more if there is no association, if it is about to be freed, or if its state is not COOKIE_WAIT, COOKIE_ECHOED or OPEN; in the remaining cases it either sends SHUTDOWN and moves to SHUTDOWN_SENT (OPEN with empty queues), sets SHUTDOWN_PENDING, or aborts the association when a user message is incomplete and the send and sent queues are empty, then (unless it aborted) calls sctp_chunk_output; the result is 0. Every path after the entry checks, including the ECONNABORTED return, ends at label out, which wakes sleepers on so_timeo and returns error.

name: sctp_release_pr_sctp_chunk
prose: Precondition: the TCB lock on stcb is held, tp1 is the chunk of the message to abandon (first chunk found in stcb's sent queue for the message), sent says whether the message had been transmitted, and so_locked says whether the caller holds the socket lock. Postcondition: it first increments the abandoned counters (abandoned_sent if sent is nonzero or tp1 is not a first fragment, abandoned_unsent otherwise) for the association, the PR-SCTP policy and the stream. Starting at tp1 it walks forward through the sent queue until it has marked a chunk that is unfragmented or has the LAST_FRAG flag (or the queue ends); for each walked chunk it adds book_size to the returned size, and, if the chunk still has data, reduces the flight size and total flight when its sent state is below SCTP_DATAGRAM_RESEND, frees the buffer space accounting, adds send_size plus sctp_peer_chunk_oh to peers_rwnd, delivers SCTP_NOTIFY_SENT_DG_FAIL (sent set) or SCTP_NOTIFY_UNSENT_DG_FAIL, frees the data and updates the removable-chunk count; every walked chunk is set to SCTP_FORWARD_TSN_SKIP and stays on the sent queue. If the end of the message was not found, it takes the chunks of the same stream and message from the head of the send queue, adding their book_size to the result, freeing buffer space (without any flight or peers_rwnd change), notifying, freeing data, setting book_size to 0 and SCTP_FORWARD_TSN_SKIP and moving them to the tail of the sent queue. If the end is still not found and the stream out queue has a pending entry sp, it sets discard_rest on it, allocates a LAST_FRAG chunk carrying the next TSN on the sent queue if no send-queue chunk was found (if that allocation fails it skips the chunk and the message-id advance), otherwise sets the LAST_FRAG flag on the chunk and advances the stream's message id, and frees sp's data (adding sp->length to the result) and updates accounting. It wakes the sending socket if anything was freed and returns the total (int); the caller keeps its locks.
note: Reviewer right (r15): flight size and peers_rwnd are only adjusted for sent-queue chunks (sctputil.c lines 5100-5107); send-queue chunks only get buffer-space, notification and data free (5158-5167). First loop adds book_size even when tp1->data is NULL (5099). Slice 4881-5181 cuts the head (function at 5065).

name: sctp_sorecvmsg
prose: Precondition: so is an SCTP socket and uio non-NULL; mp, from, sinfo and msg_flags are optional; the caller holds no socket-buffer or read-queue lock. Postcondition: it returns an errno or 0, with a single exit at the end of the function. It returns EINVAL, without any lock held, if uio is NULL or MSG_PEEK is combined with a non-NULL mp, EOPNOTSUPP if MSG_OOB is set, EFAULT if so_pcb is NULL, and, after taking the socket receive I/O lock, the error of SOCK_IO_RECV_LOCK. While looking for data it returns 0 when the endpoint socket is gone or when the receive side is shut down with nothing available (end of file; nothing copied), so_error (cleared unless MSG_PEEK) when it is set and no data is available, ECONNRESET or ENOTCONN on a TCP-style endpoint that is not connected, EWOULDBLOCK for a non-blocking call without data, or the sbwait error. When data is available it takes the first suitable control from the read queue, copies data into uio (or hands mbufs to *mp), frees consumed mbufs and controls, may wait for more data when only part of a message has arrived, and returns the error of uiomove or of a wait, or 0. At the exit it stores out_flags in *msg_flags when msg_flags is non-NULL, sets serinfo_next_flags to SCTP_NO_NEXT_MSG when MSG_EOR is not set in out_flags, the call was not a peek, sinfo is given and extended receive info is enabled, releases the read lock, socket buffer lock and receive I/O lock it holds, drops the association reference and saves freed_so_far if it applied one, may send a window update through sctp_user_rcvd, and wakes the reader if wakeup_read_socket was set.
note: Reviewer (r15) right: the so_error return exists at sctputil.c lines 5617-5621 and 5631-5636; r1/r2 point that 0 can be returned at EOF with no data copied is stated. Function is 5511-6473; slice 5435-5707 holds the end of sctp_user_rcvd and the start of this function.

name: tcp_do_segment
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inpcb write lock and is inside a network epoch (NET_EPOCH_ASSERT, INP_WLOCK_ASSERT), tp is a tcpcb in a state after TCPS_LISTEN and not TCPS_TIME_WAIT (KASSERTs), m holds the received segment, th points to its TCP header, drop_hdrlen is the header length to trim, tlen the payload length and iptos the TOS byte. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and consumes m on every path (it frees it, appends it to the socket receive buffer, or passes it to tcp_reass). It runs the segment through TCP input processing (SYN and RST handling, PAWS and options, window and sequence trimming, ACK processing with congestion control, RTT, SACK and fast recovery, window update, data queueing, FIN handling, and state changes), and may call tcp_output, tcp_close, tcp_drop, tcp_twstart or tcp_dropwithreset. It releases the inpcb write lock itself on the normal exit (INP_WUNLOCK at check_delack and dropafterack) and at the drop and dropwithreset labels when tp is non-NULL; it does not unlock where tp has been set to NULL by tcp_close or tcp_drop; and in the CLOSING and FIN_WAIT_2 cases that call tcp_twstart it returns without calling INP_WUNLOCK, tcp_twstart having released the lock. When tcp_close or tcp_drop frees tp the caller must not use it afterwards.
note: Reviewer (r15) wrong: tcp_do_segment does release the inp lock: INP_WUNLOCK at tcp_input.c lines 3390, 3418, 3425, 3435; it returns after tcp_twstart at 3071 and 3372 (tcp_twstart unlocks, tcp_timewait.c:185/190). Not read: every intermediate statement of this 1900-line function; ownership of m checked at the m_freem/sbappend/tcp_reass sites. Slice 1587-1839 cuts the head (function at 1519).
